value:
"Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI) is the Functional Genomics Data Generation Project (also described in the source documents as the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge) of the U.S. National Institutes of Health Bridge to Artificial Intelligence (Bridge2AI) program. Its stated mission is "to produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, to enable transformative biomedical AI research." CM4AI's objective is to deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-Ready data produced from multimodal interrogation of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions, using mass spectrometry based proteomics, spatial proteomics / cell imaging, and genetic perturbations using CRISPR/Cas9.
This record describes the CM4AI data release programme: the quarterly, publicly archived data releases deposited in LibraData, the University of Virginia's instance of Dataverse (an NIH-approved generalist repository). Each release is enumerated under `resources`. Input data streams comprise affinity purification mass spectrometry (AP-MS) and size exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry (SEC-MS) protein-protein interaction data, immunofluorescence (IF) subcellular imaging for spatial proteomics, and single-cell CRISPR/CRISPRi perturbation (perturb-seq) screens. Cell lines under investigation are the triple-negative breast cancer line MDA-MB-468 (treated with paclitaxel or vorinostat versus untreated) and the induced pluripotent stem cell line KOLF2.1J (undifferentiated versus iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, neurons, and cardiomyocytes). Outputs are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-Ready datasets in RO-Crate format using an extended, client-server version of the FAIRSCAPE framework.
The source documents give two different institutional lists for the collaboration. The CM4AI data-releases page states that CM4AI "is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UT Austin, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center, as part of the NIH Bridge2AI program." The March 2025, June 2025 and later Dataverse release descriptions state "CM4AI is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center" (without UT Austin). Both statements are recorded here as they appear.
The CM4AI portal reports the following aggregate "Data Insights" figures: 1,374 protein interactions; 53,788 immunofluorescent images; 7,023 total proteins investigated; 11,739 genes targeted; 21.4 TB data volume.
Both the CM4AI portal and the University of Virginia Dataverse collection display the notice: "This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives.""
reason: Genuinely descriptive prose about the dataset, though bloated with source-document provenance commentary and repository notices better placed in other fields.

value: [{"id": "d4d:CM4AI_purpose_mission", "name": "CM4AI mission", "response": "\"Its overarching mission is to produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, to enable transformative biomedical AI research.\""}, {"id": "d4d:CM4AI_purpose_objective", "name": "CM4AI objective", "response": "\"CM4AI's objective is to deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-Ready data produced from multimodal interrogation of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under perturbed and unperturbed conditions, utilizing state-of-the-art mass spectrometry based proteomics, spatial proteomics / cell imaging, and genetic perturbations using CRISPR.\""}, {"id": "d4d:CM4AI_purpose_nih_project", "name": "NIH RePORTER project purpose", "response": "\"As part of the NIH Common Fund's Bridge2AI program, the CM4AI data generation project seeks to map the spatiotemporal architecture of human cells and use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning.\" The project also states it \"will implement a standards data management approach based on FAIR access and software principles, with deep provenance and replication packages for representation of cell maps and their underlying datasets; initiate a research program in ethical AI, especially as it relates to how maps will be used in genomic medicine and model interpretation; and stimulate a diverse portfolio of training opportunities in the emerging field of biomachine learning.\""}, {"id": "d4d:CM4AI_purpose_strategic", "name": "Strategic aim", "response": "\"At a strategic level, CM4AI - as do other Bridge2AI DGPs - aims to ethically leverage the most state-of-the art computational and experimental tools in biomedical science to enable a new generation of transformative artificial intelligence research to benefit humanity. Its datasets and software are available to the research community under minimally restrictive terms consistent with ethical guidelines, researcher attribution, and research integrity.\""}]
reason: A list of well-formed Purpose objects, each stating a distinct creation goal or intended application of the dataset.

value:
"Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI; CM4AI.org) is the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge / Data Generation Project of the U.S. National Institutes of Health Bridge2AI program. Its stated mission is to produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, to enable transformative biomedical AI research, and to use these maps toward the grand challenge of interpretable genotype-phenotype learning.
This record describes the CM4AI data release series published as a collection in the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), the University of Virginia's archival data repository and an NIH-approved generalist repository. CM4AI delivers machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, together with quarterly data releases of map-input data streams. The releases carry multimodal data generated from chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders, measured in disease-relevant cell lines under treated and untreated conditions: protein-protein interaction data from affinity purification mass spectrometry (AP-MS) and size-exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry (SEC-MS); spatial proteomics from immunofluorescence (IF) confocal imaging; and single-cell CRISPR/Cas9 genetic perturbation (perturb-seq) data. The cell lines are the triple-negative breast cancer line MDA-MB-468 (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat treatment) and the induced pluripotent stem cell line KOLF2.1J (undifferentiated and differentiated to neural progenitor cells, neurons, and cardiomyocytes).
Input data streams are integrated by the Multi-Scale Integrated Cell (MuSIC) software pipeline using deep-learning embeddings and community detection, and outputs are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using an extended client-server version of the FAIRSCAPE framework, which assigns persistent ARK identifiers and computes EVI evidence-graph provenance entailments.
The CM4AI project portal reports the following aggregate figures for the data generation effort: 1,374 protein interactions; 53,788 immunofluorescent images; 7,023 total proteins investigated; 11,739 genes targeted; and 21.4 TB of data volume. CM4AI is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UT Austin, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center, as part of the NIH Bridge2AI program."
reason: Detailed, human-readable prose describing the dataset collection; correct form and substance for a description field.

value: "The Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI) data release programme is the ongoing, quarterly series of AI-ready data releases produced by CM4AI, the Functional Genomics Data Generation Project of the U.S. National Institutes of Health Bridge2AI program. CM4AI's stated objective is to deliver machine-readable hierarchical maps of cell architecture as AI-ready data, produced from multimodal interrogation of chromatin modifiers, metabolic enzymes, and other proteins involved in cancer, neuropsychiatric, and cardiac disorders in disease-relevant cell lines under treated and untreated conditions. The input data streams are generated by mass spectrometry based proteomics (affinity purification mass spectrometry, AP-MS, and size exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry, SEC-MS), spatial proteomics / immunofluorescence (IF) cell imaging, and genetic perturbation using CRISPR/Cas9 (perturb-seq). The two cell systems under investigation are the triple-negative breast cancer line MDA-MB-468 (untreated / DMSO control, paclitaxel-treated, vorinostat-treated) and the induced pluripotent stem cell line KOLF2.1J (undifferentiated parental cells and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells, neurons, and cardiomyocytes). Outputs are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using an extended client-server version of the FAIRSCAPE framework, and are deposited in LibraData, the University of Virginia's Dataverse instance and an NIH-approved generalist repository. Individual quarterly releases are recorded as `resources` of this record; the June 2026 Data Release (Beta), doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, is the current release named by the CM4AI data releases page. The CM4AI portal and data releases page report project-level \"Data Insights\" figures of 1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 total proteins investigated, 11,739 genes targeted, and a data volume of 21.4 TB."

value: "The June 2026 Data Release (Beta) of Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge in the U.S. National Institutes of Health Bridge2AI program. CM4AI generates multi-modal data including protein-protein interaction (PPI), spatial localization, and genetic perturbation data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat treatment) and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (with and without differentiation). The release record describes the Beta release as including: perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and iPSC-derived neural progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells; and immunofluorescence images in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment. The ten-file inventory of this release contains perturb-seq archives for KOLF2.1J only; the external perturb-seq links for both KOLF2.1J iPSCs and MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells are marked \"Embargoed\", so the MDA-MB-468 perturb-seq component named in the release prose is not represented among the deposited files. CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework. CM4AI is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UT Austin, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center."

value: "The June 2026 Data Release of Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI; cm4ai.org), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge in the U.S. National Institutes of Health Bridge2AI program. CM4AI generates multi-modal data including protein-protein interaction (PPI), spatial localization, and genetic perturbation data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat treatment) and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (with and without differentiation). The Dataverse release description states that this Beta release comprises: Perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and for undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and iPSC-derived neuron progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with treatment; and immunofluorescence (IF) images in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment. The deposited file inventory does not contain an MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq file and the External Data Links mark that resource as embargoed; see the anomalies section. Output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework. CM4AI is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UT Austin, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center."
